limitations: Default Vite proxy targets the hosted production API; dev token injection can read/write that service.
Single household dataset per instance; signed-in users are not separated by email at the data layer.
Custom API domains require adapting hardcoded machine-host checks as well as CLI URLs and edge Access policies.
JSON export excludes R2 bytes and API tokens but includes settings (which may include Backy secrets).
POST /api/backup currently omits D1 batch executor and fails at BEGIN TRANSACTION; not a working D1 restore path.
Current logout uses merge-writing ConfigManager and may leave saved token present; no server token revoke operation is performed.
Beneficiaries are read-only; attachments upload/file routes exist but CLI lacks upload and policy-transition subcommands.
Legacy .env.example, remote seed and old proxy plans are not current setup instructions.
Release does not apply schema changes; main checks HTTP 200 while tagged release also checks version.
